extraction_notes.note: Theorem 1', Lemmas 11' and 10' and Proposition 4' use custom manualtheorem/manuallemma/manualprop environments that latex_facts.py does not report; their \labels resolve to sections, so these nodes were cut by hand (confidence 0.9) and the edges their \refs state were added by hand with basis named.

Claims 7 and 21 are claim environments inside prose proofs whose arguments come much later (Section 8; end of Section 6.4). Step rule 7 would put the argument inside the claim node, but the environment span rule wins: the claim keeps its environment span and its argument is a separate proof node.
remark or proposition: Remark 26 states a necessary condition and proves it in its own body; kept as remark (author's word), no rigor flag since the argument is complete.
Section 7 is a proof sketch spread over three subsections; split into one proof node per sketched result (Theorem 1', Lemma 11', Lemma 10'), with the results themselves marked semi_formal.
Subsections 1.3-1.5 (history of the manuscript, organization, acknowledgement), the flowchart figure, and heuristic asides such as the remark after Lemma 8 were not extracted.

nodes.name: Kim-Vu Sandwich Conjecture
nodes.statement: The Sandwich Conjecture of Kim and Vu~\cite{KV04} claims that if $d \gg \log n$, then for some sequences $p_1 = p_1(n) \sim d/n$ and $p_2 = p_2(n) \sim d/n$ there is a joint distribution of a random $d$-regular graph $\mathbb R(n,d)$ and two binomial random graphs $\mathbb G(n,p_1)$ and $\mathbb G(n,p_2)$ such that with probability tending to $1$ \begin{equation*} \mathbb G(n,p_1) \subseteq \mathbb R(n,d) \subseteq \mathbb G(n,p_2). \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: For d >> log n, R(n,d) can be sandwiched a.a.s. between G(n,p_1) and G(n,p_2) with p_i ~ d/n.
assumptions: $d \gg \log n$
conclusions: for some sequences $p_1 = p_1(n) \sim d/n$ and $p_2 = p_2(n) \sim d/n$ there is a joint distribution of a random $d$-regular graph $\mathbb R(n,d)$ and two binomial random graphs $\mathbb G(n,p_1)$ and $\mathbb G(n,p_2)$ such that with probability tending to $1$

nodes.name: Kim-Vu partial sandwich theorem
nodes.statement: For $\log n \ll d \ll n^{1/3}(\log n)^{-2}$, Kim and Vu proved the embedding $\mathbb G(n,p_1) \subseteq \mathbb R(n,d)$ as well as an imperfect embedding $\mathbb R(n,d) \setminus H \subseteq \mathbb G(n,p_2)$, where $H$ is some pretty sparse subgraph of $\mathbb R(n,d)$.
assumptions: $\log n \ll d \ll n^{1/3}(\log n)^{-2}$
conclusions: the embedding $\mathbb G(n,p_1) \subseteq \mathbb R(n,d)$ as well as an imperfect embedding $\mathbb R(n,d) \setminus H \subseteq \mathbb G(n,p_2)$

nodes.name: Lower embedding for d << n (Dudek-Frieze-Rucinski-Sileikis)
nodes.statement: In~\cite{DFRSc} the lower embedding was extended to $d \ll n$ (and, in fact, to uniform hypergraph counterparts of the models $\mathbb G(n,p)$ and $\mathbb R(n,d)$).

nodes.name: Sandwich conjecture for large d (Gao-Isaev-McKay; Gao)
nodes.statement: Recently, Gao, Isaev, and McKay~\cite{GIM} came up with a result which confirms the conjecture for $d \gg n/\sqrt{\log n}$ (\cite{GIM} is the first paper that gives the (perfect) embedding $\mathbb R(n,d) \subseteq \mathbb G(n,p_2)$ for some range of $d$) and, subsequently, Gao~\cite{G20} widely extended this range to $d=\Omega(\log^7n)$.

nodes.name: Bipartite Erdos-Renyi random graph G(n1,n2,m)
nodes.statement: Given an integer $m \in [0, n_1n_2]$, let $\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,m)$ be an $m$-edge subgraph of $K_{n_1,n_2}$ chosen uniformly at random (the bipartite Erd\H os--R\'enyi model).

nodes.name: Binomial bipartite random graph G(n1,n2,p)
nodes.statement: Given a number $p \in [0,1]$, let $\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,p)$ be the binomial bipartite random graph where each edge of $K_{n_1,n_2}$ is included independently with probability~$p$.

nodes.name: Biregular class R(n1,n2,p) and degrees d_1, d_2
nodes.statement: If, in addition, \[ d_1 := pn_2\qquad\text{and}\qquad d_2 := pn_1 \] are integers (we shall always make this implicit assumption), we let ${\mathcal{R}}(n_1,n_2,p)$ be the class of subgraphs of $K_{n_1,n_2}$ such that every $v \in V_i$ has degree $d_i$, for $i = 1, 2$ (it is an easy exercise to show that ${\mathcal{R}}(n_1,n_2,p)$ is non-empty).
nodes.statement_short: d_1=pn_2, d_2=pn_1 (assumed integers); R(n1,n2,p) is the class of subgraphs of K_{n1,n2} with all degrees d_i on side V_i.

nodes.name: p-biregular graph
nodes.statement: We call such graphs \emph{$p$-biregular}.

nodes.name: Random biregular graph R(n1,n2,p)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbb R(n_1,n_2,p)$ be a random graph chosen uniformly from ${\mathcal{R}}(n_1,n_2,p)$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic regime min{n1,n2} -> infinity
nodes.statement: Throughout the paper we assume that the underlying complete bipartite graph $K_{n_1,n_2}$ grows on both sides, that is, $\min\{n_1,n_2\} \to \infty$, and any parameters (e.g., $p$, $m$), events, random variables, etc., are allowed to depend on $(n_1,n_2)$.

nodes.name: Asymptotically almost surely (a.a.s.)
nodes.statement: We say that an event $\mathcal E = \mathcal E(n_1,n_2)$ holds \emph{asymptotically almost surely} (\emph{a.a.s.}) if $\prob{\mathcal E} \to 1$.

nodes.name: Sandwiching in the balanced case
nodes.statement: If $p\gg\frac{\log n}{n}$ and $1 - p \gg \left( \frac{\log n}{n} \right)^{1/4}$, then for some $m \sim pn^2$ there is a joint distribution of random graphs $\mathbb G(n,n,m)$ and $\mathbb R(n,n,p)$ such that \begin{equation} \mathbb G(n,n,m) \subseteq \mathbb R(n,n,p) \qquad \text{a.a.s.} \end{equation} If $p\gg\left(\frac{\log^3 n}{n}\right)^{1/4}$, then for some $m \sim pn^2$ there is a joint distribution of random graphs $\mathbb G(n,n,m)$ and $\mathbb R(n,n,p)$ such that \begin{equation} \mathbb R(n,n,p) \subseteq \mathbb G(n,n,m) \qquad \text{a.a.s.} \end{equation} Moreover, in \eqref{eq:1stemb} and \eqref{eq:2ndemb} one can replace $\mathbb G(n,n,m)$ by the binomial random graph $\mathbb G(n,n,p')$, for some $p' \sim p$.
nodes.statement_short: Balanced case n1=n2=n: G(n,n,m) embeds in R(n,n,p) a.a.s. for log n/n << p, 1-p >> (log n/n)^{1/4}; the reverse embedding holds for p >> (log^3 n/n)^{1/4}.
assumptions: $p\gg\frac{\log n}{n}$ and $1 - p \gg \left( \frac{\log n}{n} \right)^{1/4}$
$p\gg\left(\frac{\log^3 n}{n}\right)^{1/4}$

nodes.name: Lower embedding G(n,n,m) in R(n,n,p) a.a.s.
nodes.statement: \mathbb G(n,n,m) \subseteq \mathbb R(n,n,p) \qquad \text{a.a.s.}
nodes.label: eq:1stemb

nodes.name: Upper embedding R(n,n,p) in G(n,n,m) a.a.s.
nodes.statement: \mathbb R(n,n,p) \subseteq \mathbb G(n,n,m) \qquad \text{a.a.s.}
nodes.label: eq:2ndemb

nodes.name: Necessity of p >> log n / n
nodes.statement: The condition $p \gg (\log n)/n$ is necessary for~\eqref{eq:1stemb} to hold with $m \sim pn^2$ (see Remark~\ref{rem_best_gamma}), since otherwise the maximum degree of $\mathbb G(n,n,m)$ is no longer $pn(1+o(1))$ a.a.s.

nodes.name: Notation N, q, n-hat, p-hat and indicator I
nodes.statement: We further write $N := n_1n_2$, $q := 1 - p$, $\hat n := \min \left\{ n_1, n_2 \right\}$, $\hat p := \min \{p, q\}$, and let \begin{equation} \mathbb I :=\mathbb I(n_1,n_2,p)= \begin{cases} 1, & \hat p < 2\frac{n_1n_2^{-1} + n_1^{-1}n_2}{\log N}\\ 0, & \hat p \ge 2\frac{n_1n_2^{-1} + n_1^{-1}n_2}{\log N}. \end{cases} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: N=n1 n2, q=1-p, n-hat=min(n1,n2), p-hat=min(p,q); I=1 iff p-hat is below 2(n1/n2+n2/n1)/log N.

nodes.name: Indicator I(n1,n2,p) of unbalanced/sparse regime
nodes.statement: \mathbb I :=\mathbb I(n_1,n_2,p)= \begin{cases} 1, & \hat p < 2\frac{n_1n_2^{-1} + n_1^{-1}n_2}{\log N}\\ 0, & \hat p \ge 2\frac{n_1n_2^{-1} + n_1^{-1}n_2}{\log N}. \end{cases}
nodes.label: eq_defI

nodes.name: Consequences of I=0
nodes.statement: Note that $\mathbb I=0$ entails that the vertex classes are rather balanced: the ratio of their sizes cannot exceed $\tfrac 1 4 \log N$. Moreover, $\mathbb I=0$ implies that $\hat p \ge 4/\log N$.

nodes.name: Embedding G(n1,n2,m) into the random biregular graph
nodes.statement: For every constant $C > 0$, there is a constant $C^*$ such that whenever the parameter $p \in [0,1]$ satisfies \begin{equation} q \ge 680\left( \frac{3(C + 4)\log N}{\hat n}\right)^{1/4} \end{equation} and \begin{equation} 1\ge\gamma := \begin{cases} C^* \left( p^2 \mathbb I + \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{p\hat n }}\right), \quad & p \le 0.49 \\ C^* \left( q^{3/2}\mathbb I + \left(\frac{\log N}{\hat n} \right)^{1/4} + \frac1q\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{\hat n}} \log \frac{\hat n}{\log N}\right), \quad & p > 0.49, \end{cases} \end{equation} there is, for $m := \lceil(1-\gamma)pN\rceil$, a joint distribution of random graphs $\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,m)$ and $\mathbb R(n_1,n_2,p)$ such that \begin{equation} \prob{\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,m) \subseteq \mathbb R(n_1,n_2,p)} = 1 - O(N^{-C}). \end{equation} If, in addition $\gamma \le 1/2$, then for $p' := (1 - 2\gamma)p$, there is a joint distribution of $\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,p')$ and $\mathbb R(n_1,n_2,p)$ such that \begin{equation} \prob{\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,p') \subseteq \mathbb R(n_1,n_2,p)} = 1 - O(N^{-C}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Under a lower bound on q and gamma<=1, G(n1,n2,m) with m=ceil((1-gamma)pN) can be coupled inside R(n1,n2,p) w.p. 1-O(N^{-C}); likewise G(n1,n2,(1-2gamma)p) if gamma<=1/2.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 3
nodes.statement: The assumptions of Corollary \ref{cor_embed} yield the assumptions of Theorem~\ref{thm_embed} with $\gamma=\bar\gamma$ and with $p$ and $q$ swapped. Note also that \[ m = \lceil(1-\bar\gamma)qN\rceil =\lceil N-pN-\bar\gamma q N\rceil= N - \lfloor(p+\bar\gamma q)N\rfloor=N-\bar m. \] Thus, by Theorem~\ref{thm_embed}, with probability $1 - O(N^{-C})$ we have $\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,N - \bar m) \subseteq \mathbb R(n_1,n_2,q)$, which, by taking complements, translates into~\eqref{eq_inverse_embed}. Similarly \[ p' = (1 - 2\bar \gamma)q N = N - (p + 2\bar \gamma q) N = N - p'' N. \] Thus, by Theorem~\ref{thm_embed}, with probability $1 - O(N^{-C})$ we have $\mathbb G(n_1,n_2,N-p''N) \subseteq \mathbb R(n_1,n_2,q)$, which, by taking complements yields embedding~\eqref{eq:inverse_Gnp}.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Theorem 2 to the complement with p and q swapped and take complements.
